title: fix(app-shell): Setup's permission-set and position holders offer Add and Remove only under the grant the server asks (objectui#12082)
body:
Fixes #12082

Clause-②: no

The census's last four `unmapped` write sites are Setup's permission-set and position holders. They are graded on measured reach, per triage's leg-B rule on the card. All four are reachable without the grant, so each becomes `mapped` to an existing row of the map. `WRITE_SITES` now holds no `unmapped` entry, which is the card's done-when. Reviewer note (e) of the previous round's contract review rides along.

## Reach, measured per site

Triage's likely case was that Setup's own gate is the boundary. Measured, it is not.

- **The four sites.** `addUsers` and `removeUser` in `AssignedUsersSection` write `sys_user_permission_set` rows. `addHolders` and `removeHolder` in `PositionHoldersSection` write `sys_user_position` rows. None read a grant.
- **Where they mount.** The permission-set editor (`PermissionMatrixEditPage`, environment scope, not embedded) and the position editor (`ResourceEditPage`'s `ENVIRONMENT_SECTIONS`). A third mount is the `sys_permission_set` record page (`RecordPermissionAssignmentsRenderer`). The catalog scope is documented as "a VIEW scope, never an authority" (`catalog-scope.ts`).
- **Setup's own gate**, read on objectstack `main` at `570f01d27`. The Setup app asks `requiredPermissions: ['setup.access']`. Its Access Control entries `Positions` and `Permission Sets`, contributed by plugin-security, carry no `requiredPermissions`. They link to `/apps/setup/metadata/position?scope=environment` and `/apps/setup/metadata/permission?scope=environment`.
- **Who reaches them without the grant.** The shipped `organization_admin` set lists `setup.access` in its `systemPermissions`. Its `objects` pin `sys_user_permission_set` and `sys_user_position` to `allowRead: true` with every write bit false. objectstack pins that in `objects/rbac-objects.test.ts` as `organization_admin is read-only on global RBAC tables to prevent privilege escalation`. `auto-org-admin-grant.ts` grants that set, or its derived wall-less variant `organization_admin_no_bypass` (same per-object entries), to every organization owner or admin member.
- **The server's answer.** The security middleware runs the delegated-administration gate first. Then it runs its step "2. CRUD permission check" for every caller, through `checkObjectPermission`. `OPERATION_TO_PERMISSION` maps `insert` to `allowCreate` and `delete` to `allowDelete`. `resolveObjectPermission` answers a set's explicit entry before its `'*'` wildcard. So that administrator's insert or delete of a grant or holding row is refused with `PERMISSION_DENIED`. The walled variant passes the delegated gate as a tenant admin and stops at step 2. The wall-less variant already stops at the gate.
- **The client is told the same.** `/me/permissions` keeps that explicit entry, because the super-user fold (`foldSuperUserWildcardGrants`) skips an object the set names. `MePermissionsProvider` answers `can()` from the explicit entry before `'*'`.
- **The objects' posture.** Both objects are `managedBy: 'system-data'` (full CRUD by bucket default), and their `apiMethods` include `create` and `delete`. No admin-only posture refuses the write before the grant does.
- **Live HTTP measurement: NOT MEASURED.** Reason: there is no built objectstack stack in this container. The reading above comes from objectstack `main` source and objectstack's own pin.

## What changes

- **The two sections read two existing rows of `AFFORDANCE_GRANTS`.** Each row is asked of the section's assignment object, with the schema `useMetadata().objects` registers and with `usePermissions()`.
  - Add reads `relatedNew`: it creates a junction row under the item, as a related list's Add existing with a link field does.
  - Remove reads `relatedRowDelete`: it deletes one.
  - A closed row withholds the Add button, the picker that button opens, and each row's Remove. The holders still list.
  - With no permission provider, every grant reads open, as before. Gating inside each component covers every mount.
- **The census.** It grades the four sites `mapped`, with the reading as the reason. `UNMAPPED_BACKLOG` is empty. The `unmapped` helper lost its last caller and retires. The freeze still turns any new `unmapped` entry red.
- **No published value widens.** No row is added to `AFFORDANCE_GRANTS`, and no export, prop or type changes. So the claim's predicted `Clause-②: no` holds as measured.
- **Docs.**
  - `packages/core/README.md`: the reuse sentence names both sections and their rows, and the backlog sentence says the pin now holds it empty.
  - `packages/app-shell/README.md`: the Setup catalog section says the holders' Add and Remove read the grant, which replaces "Assigning holders stays writable".
  - `PositionHoldersSection`'s docblock no longer says a tenant administrator assigns under a wall.
- **Changeset.** `.changeset/12082-setup-holders-grant.md` declares `@object-ui/app-shell: patch`. `plugin-form` changes one test file, and `core` only its README.

## Reviewer note (e)

`RecordDetailView.feedGrant-12082.test.tsx` gains one case. It mounts the record page with the registered `sys_comment` and `sys_comment_reaction` schemas in the page's `objects`: their `managedBy`, `userActions` and `enable` blocks, as objectstack's `plugin-audit` declares them. The reaction object's effective operation set comes from the spec's own `resolveEffectiveApiMethods` and `effectiveOperationsArray`, applied to that `enable` block. Under a full grant the composer, the reaction add and the take-back are each offered, so the registered policy closes nothing the feed offers.

## Tests and gates, at head `7e9eed3`

The head is the merge of `origin/main` `dcd1041` into `4754b38`. Locally, only the targeted subset ran. The farm is CI's.

- **Suites.** `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` over 43 files: `Test Files 43 passed (43)`, `Tests 373 passed (373)`, exit 0. The files are:
  - the census pin;
  - the new `setupHoldersGrant-12082.test.tsx`;
  - the existing `AssignedUsersSection` and `PositionHoldersSection` suites;
  - every `PermissionMatrixEditor.*` suite;
  - the environment-scope and permission-reading `ResourceEditPage`, catalog and gate suites in `metadata-admin`, plus `PermissionAdvancedFacets.adminScopeAnchor` from the merge;
  - the two feed suites, `useApproverDirectory.contractEnvelope-5945`, and app-shell's ratchet suites.
- **Build.** `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell...'`: 29 tasks successful, exit 0.
- **Type-check.** `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` exit 0. `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-form type-check` exit 0. Each runs `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, and that test program includes `src/**/*.test.tsx`.
- **Lint.** eslint on the five changed source and test files: 0 errors. One warning sits on an added line: the pre-existing `onSelectRecords` `any`, re-indented under `canAdd`. The files are byte-identical between `4754b38` and `7e9eed3`.
- **Lock-free gates.**
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: exit 0.
  - `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: exit 0, `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)`.
  - A raw control-byte scan of the changed files: none.
- **`pnpm check:readme-exports`: exit 1, a partial reading.** It could not judge 72 self-imports. All of them sit in packages outside the built closure (cli, plugin-ai, plugin-gantt, plugin-map, plugin-markdown, plugin-timeline). None of its findings names `packages/core/README.md` or `packages/app-shell/README.md`. CI's `README Export Check` gives the whole-tree verdict.
- **Not run locally.** The rest of the 510-file `metadata-admin` directory, and the rest of the farm. A first run over the whole directory was stopped by me before reporting, to free the shared lock. It is NOT MEASURED.

## Ablations (one-time, not committed)

Each ran through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode, at `4754b38`. In each, the anchor hit once and the mutation landed (the blob changed). After the run, the restore was proved: the blob matches `HEAD` and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

- **A1.** `AssignedUsersSection`'s `canAdd` set to `true`. Red as expected: 4 of the section's 7 cases fail (the organization administrator, read-only, delete-only, and operation-set cases). So does the census's `every mapped site names rows of the map, of its own verb, each read by one of the files it names`. Overall: `Tests 5 failed | 58 passed (63)`.
- **A2.** `PositionHoldersSection`'s `canRemove` set to `true`. Red as expected: 4 cases (the organization administrator, read-only, create-only, and operation-set cases) plus the same census assertion. Overall: `Tests 5 failed | 58 passed (63)`.
- **A3.** The new note (e) case's registered `sys_comment` schema given `userActions: { create: false }`. Red as expected: only the new case fails, on `expect(composer(view)).not.toBeNull()` (`Tests 1 failed | 18 passed (19)`). That shows the case reads the registered schemas from the page's `objects`. The first A3 attempt was a no-op and is void: its replacement carried its own anchor, so the tool refused and restored.

## Acceptance notes

- **The object grant only.** Each section reads the object grant, which is a necessary condition of the write. It does not read the delegated-administration gate, which can still refuse a holder of the grant: no covering `adminScope`, a business unit outside the scope's subtree, or a set off its allowlist. Every row of the map has the same object-verdict posture.
- **A dead mount.** `RecordPermissionAssignmentsRenderer` mounts on the `sys_permission_set` record page. objectstack `main` no longer registers that object (its migration entry `catalog-row-objects-retired`), so that mount cannot load against a current server. It is read here only because the gate sits inside the shared component. It is not filed and has no carrier.
- **A contradiction in objectstack, reported to the seat and not filed here.** The migration entry `walled-catalog-tenant-writes-retired` says, in its replacement text, that an organization's administrators assign the catalog to their members through `sys_user_position` and `sys_user_permission_set`, "which are unchanged". The shipped `organization_admin` set is read-only on both. This PR follows the set the server enforces.
- **Partial grants.** A grant with create but not delete gets Add and no Remove, and the reverse, as the split cases pin.
